data.narrative:
Ohalo Genetics operates in Robotics & Manufacturing at the Series C stage. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine comparable companies—one public and eight private—including three direct Stage C comparables (Hadrian, Agile Robots, Nimble Robotics) alongside broader sector references such as Divergent and Exotec.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the company's $205M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, implying a valuation of $348M. The peer-median method benchmarks against three same-sector, same-stage competitors with a median valuation of $1.0B and a range spanning $1.0B to $1.6B, directly implying $1.0B. These peers represent the most comparable reference set available.

Synthesizing both approaches yields a triangulated range of $296M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $674M. The substantial spread reflects tension between the stage-progression method anchored to raised capital and peer multiples that suggest materially higher valuations for comparable-stage robotics companies. Key uncertainties include whether Ohalo's capital efficiency and market position warrant a premium or discount to peer medians, and whether the peer set adequately reflects company-specific risk factors. The $674M midpoint represents a reasonable synthesis, though resolution toward either bound depends on due diligence around unit economics and competitive positioning within the peer cohort.
